text:
ani: Heads-up from today's canary: two tricky handoff modes popped up that we should nail down for the hosted/dedicated/private handshake. Notably: (A) whether hosted may proxy tenant creds during fallback, and (B) how KV namespaces move when a binding changes.

kevin: Saw the same. For (A) I'm leaning to NEVER forward customer KMS creds to hosted; use a scoping service-principal instead and emit orig_tenant in telemetry. Forwarding increases blast radius.

lee: Agreed on principle, but dedicated->hosted fallbacks for low-latency customers want minimal friction. Service-principal must support per-tenant scoped scopes so billing/observability still works.

sophia: Proposal: handshake manifest includes fields: cred_strategy: [forward|service_principal|require_rebind], cache_move: [flush|namespace_swap|tombstone], rebind_grace_seconds, audit_level. Default safe values: cred_strategy=require_rebind, cache_move=namespace_swap, rebind_grace_seconds=30.

ani: Can we show a tiny example?

kevin: Example:
```yaml
handshake:
  flow: hosted->private
  cred_strategy: service_principal
  cache_move: namespace_swap
  rebind_grace_seconds: 45
  audit_level: high
```

lee: Runtime semantics for namespace_swap: create new namespace id, route new writes there, reads check header `X-Cache-Epoch` and reject if epoch < current. Tombstone = allow reads for grace period then evict. Flush = immediate eviction (fast but risky).

sophia: Add events: handshake.request, handshake.bind_accepted, handshake.bind_refused(reason), cache.epoch_roll(old->new), creds.issued(method). Include tenant_id and correlation_id in each event.

audit-bot: audit-bot: canary "handshake-probe-epoch" ran on staging at 14:02 UTC :white_check_mark:

ani: Action items: sophia to update RFC with manifest schema and defaults; kevin to draft telemetry mapping for service_principal fallbacks; lee to write SDK helper that returns a deterministic state-machine stream (on_quiesce/on_bind/on_fail). We'll keep defaults conservative and relax after perf runs.

kevin: Also add a short section about operator overrides: infra can permit forward for legacy tenants behind a flag, but must log explicit approval and rotate keys.
